NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION

  Public Comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If you would like to

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MARCH 25, 2025

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR STEGURA called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Aeris Pranin, student from Rancho Vista Elementary.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Pettit

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MARCH 2025 AS WOMEN’S HISTORY MONTH

MAYOR STEGURA declared March 2025 as Women’s History Month and invited Palos Verdes
Peninsula League of Women Voters president Nancy Mahr and past president Linda Herman
to the podium to accept the proclamation.

MAYOR STEGURA presented the Mayor’s award to Rancho Vista Elementary student Aeris
Pranin for her science fair project.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-L AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

  APPROVED.

  WARRANTS 020525 THROUGH 020625; 030125 THROUGH 030325 IN THE

  REGIONAL PUBLIC AFFAIRS PROGRAM MANAGER

Kimberly Caballero, Cal Water Regional Public Affairs Manager provided a presentation on the
Palos Verdes water system, major infrastructure improvements completed in recent years, and
emergency preparedness measures.

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: PILOT PROGRAM FOR ALL-
  DAY TENNIS CLUB COURT RESERVATIONS AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 25, 2025
   Recommendation: That the City Council review and approve the proposed six-month
  pilot program beginning May 19, 2025 for all-day tennis club court reservations at
  Ernie Howlett Park.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant City Manager Davis confirmed members can also make pickleball reservations,
and discussed the charges for court reservations, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
HUFF.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE PROPOSED SIX-MONTH PILOT PROGRAM BEGINNING
  MAY 19, 2025 FOR ALL-DAY TENNIS CLUB COURT RESERVATIONS AT
  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH MATRIX CONSULTING GROUP
  TO CONDUCT A FEE STUDY FOR THE COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a Professional Services Agreement
  with Matrix Consulting Group in the amount of $17,000 for a comprehensive fee study
  of the Community Services Department to the satisfaction of the City Attorney.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH MATRIX
  CONSULTING GROUP IN THE AMOUNT OF $17,000 FOR A
  COMPREHENSIVE FEE STUDY OF THE COMMUNITY SERVICES
  DEPARTMENT TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

C.  RESOLUTION NO. 2595 APPROVING THE BLANKET AUTHORITY TO FILE
  APPLICATIONS FOR MEASURE A ANNUAL ALLOCATION GRANT FUNDS AND
  APPROVAL OF THE MEASURE A ANNUAL ALLOCATION GRANT AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2595, granting the City
  Manager authority to file applications for Measure A grant funding and authorize the
  City Manager to sign the Measure A Annual Allocation Grant Master Agreement
  between the City and Los Angeles County Regional Parks and Open Space District.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 25, 2025
   ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2595, GRANTING THE CITY MANAGER
  AUTHORITY TO FILE APPLICATIONS FOR MEASURE A GRANT FUNDING
  AND AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO SIGN THE MEASURE A ANNUAL
  ALLOCATION GRANT MASTER AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY AND
  LOS ANGELES COUNTY REGIONAL PARKS AND OPEN SPACE DISTRICT.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2595 by title.

D.  2024 HOUSING ELEMENT AND GENERAL PLAN ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to submit the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates’ 2024 General Plan and Housing Element Annual Progress Reports (APRs)
  to the Governor’s Office of Planning and Research (OPR) and the Department of
  Housing and Community Development (HCD) by April 1, 2025.

Community Services Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Community Services Director Naughton explained how the rent calculations are made, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO SUBMIT THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES’ 2024
  GENERAL PLAN AND HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS
  REPORTS (APRS) TO THE GOVERNOR’S OFFICE OF PLANNING AND
  RESEARCH (OPR) AND THE DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT (HCD) BY APRIL 1, 2025.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: RELOCATE THE PLANNED
  DEEP VALLEY DRIVE CROSSWALK AND BULB-OUT FROM THE LIBRARY MAIN
  ENTRANCE TO THE 627 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE MIXED-USE RESIDENTIAL
  BUILDING (LA COLLINA); AND APPROVE AN AMENDMENT TO WILLDAN TASK
  ORDER 2024-13

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Approve the relocation of the proposed
  crosswalk and bulb-out from the main entrance to the library on Deep Valley Drive to
  the location in front of Reverent Coffee, located at 627 Deep Valley Drive, as shown
  on the attached exhibit; and, revise the bulb-out design on the south side of Deep
  Valley Drive, to extend farther to the west to allow for the parking one vehicle to the
  west of the bulb-out by adjusting the traffic lane configuration on Deep Valley Drive;
  and, 2) Approve an amendment to Task Order No. 2024-13 with Willdan in the
  amount of $32,785, for additional pedestrian crossing engineering design services
  under the Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP).

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received by Dan Houk, Vice President of the La Collina Homeowners
Association, who expressed his gratitude to the City Council, Traffic and Safety Committee and
staff, for their responsiveness to the petition to relocate the crosswalk. He thanked Public
Works Director Wahba for being receptive to his concerns and Council Member Schachter for
helping to guide him through the City’s process.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 25, 2025
   COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  1) APPROVE THE RELOCATION OF THE PROPOSED CROSSWALK AND
  BULB-OUT FROM THE MAIN ENTRANCE TO THE LIBRARY ON DEEP
  VALLEY DRIVE TO THE LOCATION IN FRONT OF REVERENT COFFEE,
  LOCATED AT 627 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE, AS SHOWN ON THE ATTACHED
  EXHIBIT; AND, REVISE THE BULB-OUT DESIGN ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF
  DEEP VALLEY DRIVE, TO EXTEND FARTHER TO THE WEST TO ALLOW
  FOR THE PARKING ONE VEHICLE TO THE WEST OF THE BULB-OUT BY
  ADJUSTING THE TRAFFIC LANE CONFIGURATION ON DEEP VALLEY
  DRIVE.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  2) APPROVE AN AMENDMENT TO TASK ORDER NO. 2024-13 WITH
  WILLDAN IN THE AMOUNT OF $32,785, FOR ADDITIONAL PEDESTRIAN
  CROSSING ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES UNDER THE HIGHWAY
  SAFETY IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM (HSIP).

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF will be attending the Cal Cities Environmental Quality Policy
Committee meeting on Friday, March 28.

MAYOR STEGURA attended the monthly Clean Power Alliance Board meeting, Peninsula
Mayor’s lunch, and the Los Angeles County Sanitation Districts Board meeting. She also
volunteered to be part of the South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG)
subcommittee for the proposed Housing Trust. MAYOR STEGURA also reported that the
Environmental Advisory Committee will meet on March 26, and that she and other
Councilmembers and staff plan to attend the SBCCOG General Assembly on Thursday, March
27.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

None.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:15 p.m. MAYOR STEGURA adjourned the meeting in memory of Fred Bayer and Susan
Morrow. The meeting was adjourned to Tuesday, April 8, 2025, at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose
of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Debby Stegura, Mayor
